observations: Two close-up photos of a metal turbocharger assembly, heavily oxidized and coated in grime/surface rust.
Red and black rubber/silicone hoses attached to intake and oil lines, both hoses look weathered, cracked, and stained.
A worn, discolored actuator/wastegate arm visible on the side of the unit, missing any clear paint or finish.
No manufacturer logo, part number, or data plate is legible in either photo.
Background is a rough concrete/plastered wall, consistent with an outdoor storage or workshop yard.
A semi-transparent watermark reading 'DNL EQUIPMENT SALES AND POSTED ON ...' overlays both images.

claims.evidence: No CAT logo, casting marks, or part/model number are visible in photo 0 or photo 1; claim cannot be confirmed from the images alone.

risks.risk: Unconfirmed fitment to a Caterpillar C9 engine (could be a generic or different-model turbo mislabeled).
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the casting/part number or Caterpillar logo stamped on the compressor housing or turbine flange.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic/unbranded used turbocharger, not CAT-specific

risks.risk: Internal condition unknown (shaft play, bearing wear, turbine blade damage, actuator function).
risks.proof: Video showing the turbine/compressor wheel spun by hand to show free, smooth rotation with no scraping or excess play.

risks.risk: Visible rust and hose degradation may indicate prolonged outdoor storage, affecting seals and internal corrosion.
risks.proof: Photo of the internal bore/wheel after removing hoses, showing no pitting or rust ingress.
risks.if_unproven: priced as heavily weathered with uncertain seal integrity

risks.risk: Possible missing or damaged mounting studs, gaskets, or the wastegate linkage seen loose in photo 0/1.
risks.proof: Close-up of mounting flange and wastegate arm showing intact hardware and linkage pivot.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming missing/damaged hardware requiring replacement

proof_requests: Clear photo of any stamped part number, casting number, or Caterpillar logo on the turbo housing.
Video of the turbine/compressor wheel being spun by hand to demonstrate free rotation.
Photo of the full unit from multiple angles showing all ports, studs, and the wastegate actuator intact.
Any paperwork, invoice, or removal photo showing it came off a C9 engine.
response.reason: The item is clearly a used turbocharger assembly, but no plate, logo, or part number is visible to confirm the Caterpillar C9 claim or its internal working condition, so it must be priced as an unverified-fitment, unverified-function used turbocharger until further proof is supplied.
